arxiv-2112-11549.title: A solar coronal loop in a box: Energy generation and heating
arxiv-2112-11549.creator: C. Breu, H. Peter, R. Cameron, S.K. Solanki, D. Przybylski, M. Rempel, L.P. Chitta
arxiv-2112-11549.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by C. Breu, H. Peter, R. Cameron, S.K. Solanki, D. Przybylski, M. Rempel, L.P. Chitta. Coronal loops are the basic building block of the upper solar atmosphere as seen in the extreme UV and X-rays. Comprehending how these are energized, structured, and evolve is key to understanding stellar coronae. Here we investigate how the energy to heat the loop is generated by photospheric magneto-convection, transported into the upper atmosphere, and how the internal structure of a coronal magnetic loop forms.

arxiv-2407-04409.title: The Fibonacci-Fubini and Lucas-Fubini numbers
arxiv-2407-04409.creator: Yahia Djemmada 1 , Abdelghani Mehdaoui 2 , László Németh 3 , and László Szalay 4
arxiv-2407-04409.description: Abstract Based on the combinatorial interpretation of the ordered Bell numbers, which count all the ordered partitions of the set [ n ] = { 1 , 2 , … , n } [n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\} , we introduce the Fibonacci partition as a Fibonacci permutation of its blocks.

arxiv-2407-08584.title: Data-Locality-Aware Task Assignment and Scheduling for Distributed Job Executions
arxiv-2407-08584.creator: Hailiang Zhao, Xueyan Tang, Peng Chen, Jianwei Yin, and Shuiguang Deng
arxiv-2407-08584.description: Abstract This paper investigates a data-locality-aware task assignment and scheduling problem aimed at minimizing job completion times for distributed job executions. Without prior knowledge of future job arrivals, we propose an optimal balanced task assignment algorithm (OBTA) that minimizes the completion time of each arriving job. We significantly reduce OBTA’s computational overhead by narrowing the search space of potential solutions.

arxiv-2409-14451.description: Abstract We present existence results for weak solutions to a broad class of degenerate McKean-Vlasov equations with rough coefficients, expanding upon and refining the techniques recently introduced by the third author. arxiv-2502-11186.title: Development of Fast Front-End Electronics for the Muon Trigger Detector in the PSI muEDM Experiment
arxiv-2502-11186.creator: Tianqi Hu, Guan Ming Wong, Chavdar Dutsov, Siew Yan Hoh, Kim Siang Khaw, Diego Alejandro Sanz Becerra, Philipp Schmidt-Wellenburg, Yuzhi Shang, and Yusuke Takeuchi

arxiv-2505-19398.title: Erasing Concepts, Steering Generations: A Comprehensive Survey of Concept Suppression PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
arxiv-2505-19398.creator: Yiwei Xie, Ping Liu, Zheng Zhang
arxiv-2505-19398.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yiwei Xie, Ping Liu, Zheng Zhang. Text-to-Image (T2I) models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in generating high-quality and diverse visual content from natural language prompts. However, uncontrolled reproduction of sensitive, copyrighted, or harmful imagery poses serious ethical, legal, and safety challenges. To address these concerns, the concept erasure paradigm has emerged as a promising direction, enabling the selective removal of specific semantic concepts from generative models while preserving their overall utility.

arxiv-2507-12296.title: Humans are more gullible than LLMs in believing common psychological myths
arxiv-2507-12296.creator: Bevan Koopman, Guido Zuccon
arxiv-2507-12296.description: Abstract Despite widespread debunking, many psychological myths remain deeply entrenched. This paper investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) mimic human behaviour of myth belief and explores methods to mitigate such tendencies. Using 50 popular psychological myths, we evaluate myth belief across multiple LLMs under different prompting strategies, including retrieval-augmented generation and swaying prompts.

arxiv-2602-08099.title: VidVec: Unlocking Video MLLM Embeddings for Video–Text Retrieval
arxiv-2602-08099.creator: Issar Tzachor, Dvir Samuel, Rami Ben-Ari
arxiv-2602-08099.description: Abstract Recent studies have adapted generative Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) into embedding extractors for vision tasks, typically through fine-tuning to produce universal representations. However, their performance on video remains inferior to Video Foundation Models (VFMs). In this paper, we focus on leveraging MLLMs for video–text embedding and retrieval.

pmc-11320938.title: Development and validation of a patient-centered communication scale for nurses
pmc-11320938.creator: Youngshin Joo, Yeonsoo Jang, Chang Gi Park, You Lee Yang
pmc-11320938.description: BackgroundPatient-centered care aims to prevent disease and promote well-being by actively involving patients in treatment and decision-making that is based on respecting the patients and their families. However, no scales have been developed to assess patient-centered care from the nurse’s perspective.

pmc-11525650.title: Synaptic changes in psychiatric and neurological disorders: state-of-the art of in vivo imaging
pmc-11525650.creator: Oliver Howes, Julia Marcinkowska, Federico E Turkheimer, Richard Carr
pmc-11525650.description: Synapses are implicated in many neuropsychiatric illnesses. Here, we provide an overview of in vivo techniques to index synaptic markers in patients. Several positron emission tomography (PET) tracers for synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2 A (SV2A) show good reliability and selectivity.

pmc-11712751.title: IUSM‐Purdue TREAT‐AD Center Capabilities and Strategy to Enable and Advance Novel Therapeutic Targets for the Treatment of Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11712751.creator: Stephanie A Mowery, Kun Huang, Andrew D Mesecar, Jeffrey L Dage, Brent Clayton, Bruce T Lamb, Alan D Palkowitz, Timothy I Richardson
pmc-11712751.description: BackgroundThe TaRget Enablement to Accelerate Therapy Development of Alzheimer’s Disease (TREAT‐AD) Centers are dedicated to identifying and validating targets from the NIH Accelerating Medicines Partnership for Alzheimer’s Disease (AMP‐AD). The centers develop Target Enabling Packages (TEPs) to explore new therapeutic target hypotheses, moving beyond the traditional focus on amyloid or tau pathologies.

pmc-11862663.title: Dismantling task-sharing psychosocial interventions to personalize care for people affected by common mental disorders: developing a taxonomy of active ingredients and ranking their efficacy
pmc-11862663.creator: D. Papola, V. Patel, C. Barbui
pmc-11862663.description: IntroductionThe global burden associated with common mental disorders is high, especially for people living in low resource settings. Although psychosocial interventions delivered by locally available lay or community health workers are effective, mechanisms of intervention response are poorly understood. One of the greatest barriers is that psychosocial interventions are administered as complex, multi-component “packages of care”.

pmc-12487597.title: Time‐restricted feeding combined with exercise improves hepatic and glycaemic metabolism in obese mice: A sex‐dependent study
pmc-12487597.creator: Gabriel Calheiros Antunes, Camila Venturini Ayres Cunha, Leandro Kansuke Oharomari, Renan Fudoli Lins Vieira, Maura Fanti, Thaiane da Silva Rios, Luciana Renata Conceição de Mattis, Ana Paula Azevêdo Macêdo, Adelino Sanchez Ramos da Silva, Eduardo Rochete Ropelle, Dennys Esper Cintra, José Rodrigo P
pmc-12487597.description: Erratic feeding patterns, such as those experienced by shift workers, can exacerbate obesity and metabolic‐associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Both nutritional factors and sexual dimorphism influence the progression of MAFLD. Time‐restricted feeding (TRF) has emerged as a promising strategy to mitigate the effects of obesity, supported by evidence of its benefits for metabolic disorders like MAFLD.

pmc-12497857.title: Targeting tumor-associated macrophages in non-small cell lung cancer: mechanisms, prognosis, and therapeutic opportunities
pmc-12497857.creator: Dameng Hao, Shengjie Chen
pmc-12497857.description: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the most prevalent and lethal form of lung cancer worldwide. Among the diverse components of the tumor microenvironment, tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are increasingly recognized as key regulators of NSCLC progression, metastasis, and treatment resistance. TAMs, particularly those polarized toward the M2-like phenotype, facilitate tumor growth through immunosuppression, angiogenesis, epithelial–mesenchymal transition, and extracellular matrix remodeling.

pmc-12862398.title: The Effect of Resistance Training on Serum Levels of Lipid Profile and Liver Enzymes in Male Rat Undergoing Radiotherapy
pmc-12862398.creator: Mohammad Parastesh, Mohammad Reza Bayatiani, Fatemeh Seif, Zahra Yuosofvand, Narges Abili
pmc-12862398.description: Background: This study investigated the effects of resistance training on lipid profiles and liver enzyme levels in male rats exposed to x-ray radiation. Methods: In this experimental study, 24 eight-week-old Sprague Dawley rats (200-250g) were randomly assigned into four groups: healthy control, irradiated control, healthy resistance training, and irradiated resistance training.

pmc-13582754.title: Learning Communities in Medical Education: Impact, Integration, and Best Practices
pmc-13582754.creator: Calvin L. Gruss, William B. Cutrer, Amy E. Fleming, Kendra Parekh, Elizabeth Ann Yakes
pmc-13582754.description: Learning communities (LCs) are longitudinal, relationship-centered structures that foster belonging, mentorship, and collaboration across diverse educational settings. This monograph focuses on LCs in undergraduate medical education (UME), summarizing their structures and models; evidence for effects on the learning environment, advising, well-being, and clinical skills; and practical strategies for implementation.
